title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a case of synthetic media used as political speech, where generated video was published to a social platform under the implied claim that a real person had said the words shown. The failure sits at the point of publication rather than in any model: a fabricated clip of a candidate was posted to X and presented as if it were her, with no label or disclosure separating the fabrication from authentic footage. Catching it would have required the platform or the poster to mark the content as synthetic at the moment of upload, since the falsity is not detectable from the video alone by an ordinary viewer.

The mechanism is impersonation by generation. The videos show a real, named person saying things she never said, and the only corrective step described is a legal letter asserting the content is fiction and may violate state defamation law. That is a response after distribution, not a check before it.

What is not established: the letter is an allegation by Cooke's attorneys, no court has ruled on the defamation claim, and nothing in the reporting establishes Van Orden's intent beyond the posting itself.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip from Aug. 4. The letter, dated Sept. 30, says the content is fiction and could violate state defamation law.

Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum. Cooke's attorneys say they are monitoring his social media accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden responded with another AI video featuring a duck saying "Cease and desist!" Cooke lost to Van Orden by about 3 percentage points in 2024.
